import uuid

from app import crud
from app.models import UserCreate
from tests.utils.user import create_random_user, authentication_token_from_email
from tests.utils.item import create_random_item
from app.core.config import settings

CANARY = "cnry-pr-mut-delete-no-owner"


def test_delete_item_owner_isolation(client, db):
    # Owner user (user_a)
    owner_user = create_random_user(db)
    owner_headers = authentication_token_from_email(
        client=client, email=owner_user.email, db=db
    )
    # Attacker user (user_b) - normal user
    attacker_user = create_random_user(db)
    attacker_headers = authentication_token_from_email(
        client=client, email=attacker_user.email, db=db
    )

    # Create an item owned by owner_user, with CANARY in title
    item_in = {
        "title": f"{CANARY} owned item",
        "description": "some description",
    }
    # Use superuser? Actually we need to create item via owner. We can use owner headers to POST.
    resp = client.post(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/",
        headers=owner_headers,
        json=item_in,
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    item = resp.json()
    item_id = item["id"]

    # Verify attacker cannot delete item (should be 403 on base)
    del_resp = client.delete(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/{item_id}",
        headers=attacker_headers,
    )
    # On base branch this should be 403; on PR branch missing check => 200
    assert del_resp.status_code == 403, f"Expected 403, got {del_resp.status_code}"
    # Ensure item still exists (optional)
    get_resp = client.get(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/{item_id}",
        headers=owner_headers,
    )
    assert get_resp.status_code == 200
    assert get_resp.json()["title"] == item_in["title"]

scenarios.root_cause: The diff removes lines 109‑110 in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py`, which enforced that only the item’s owner or a superuser could delete it. Without this ownership check, any authenticated user can supply another user’s `id` in the path and delete that item, widening access to `DELETE /items/{id} | user_a | user_b | base` and the symmetric case — a classic Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) regression [https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization) [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html). Restore the two deleted lines (or an equivalent policy) so non‑superusers are blocked when `item.owner_id != current_user.id`.

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from tests.utils.user import authentication_token_from_email, create_random_user
from tests.utils.utils import random_lower_string


def test_user_a_cannot_see_user_b_items_canary_leak(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    # Create two distinct users
    user_a = create_random_user(db)
    user_b = create_random_user(db)
    # Ensure they are different
    assert user_a.id != user_b.id

    # Obtain headers for each user
    headers_a = authentication_token_from_email(
        client=client, email=user_a.email, db=db
    )
    headers_b = authentication_token_from_email(
        client=client, email=user_b.email, db=db
    )

    # Define the canary string
    canary = "cnry-pr-mut-list-leak"

    # User A creates an item containing the canary in title
    item_a_in = {
        "title": f"{canary}_A",
        "description": "user a item"
    }
    resp_a = client.post(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/",
        headers=headers_a,
        json=item_a_in,
    )
    assert resp_a.status_code == 200, f"User A item creation failed: {resp_a.text}"
    item_a = resp_a.json()

    # User B creates an item without the canary (different title)
    item_b_in = {
        "title": random_lower_string(),
        "description": "user b item"
    }
    resp_b = client.post(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/",
        headers=headers_b,
        json=item_b_in,
    )
    assert resp_b.status_code == 200, f"User B item creation failed: {resp_b.text}"
    item_b = resp_b.json()

    # Now user A requests the list of items
    list_resp = client.get(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/",
        headers=headers_a,
    )
    assert list_resp.status_code == 200, f"List fetch failed: {list_resp.text}"
    data = list_resp.json()
    # Assuming the response format is {"data": [...]} as seen in existing test_read_items
    items = data.get("data", data)  # fallback if format differs

    # User A should only see their own item due to owner filter.
    # If the filter is missing (regression), they will see both items.
    # Assert that exactly one item is returned (their own).
    assert len(items) == 1, f"Expected 1 item for user A, got {len(items)}: {[i.get('title') for i in items]}"
    # Additionally, ensure the canary is in the returned item's title
    titles = [i.get("title") for i in items if isinstance(i, dict)]
    assert any(canary in t for t in titles), f"Canary not found in user A's item: {titles}"

scenarios.root_cause: The removal of `.where(Item.owner_id == current_user.id)` on line 37 of `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` eliminates the owner filter from the list query, causing GET /items/ to return all items instead of only those belonging to the authenticated user. This widens the operation for both user_a and user_b, violating read-isolation (I1) and enabling Broken Object Level Authorization (API1:2023) where users can access objects by manipulating or omitting ownership checks, as described in CWE-639. import uuid
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlmodel import Session

from app import crud
from app.core.config import settings
from app.models import UserCreate
from tests.utils.user import user_authentication_headers
from tests.utils.utils import random_email, random_lower_string

CANARY = "cnry-pr-mut-mass-assign-owner"


def test_owner_id_mass_assignment_isolation(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    # Create attacker user
    email_a = random_email()
    password_a = random_lower_string()
    user_in_a = UserCreate(email=email_a, password=password_a)
    user_a = crud.create_user(session=db, user_create=user_in_a)
    headers_a = user_authentication_headers(
        client=client, email=email_a, password=password_a
    )

    # Create victim user
    email_b = random_email()
    password_b = random_lower_string()
    user_in_b = UserCreate(email=email_b, password=password_b)
    user_b = crud.create_user(session=db, user_create=user_in_b)
    victim_id = user_b.id

    # Attacker attempts to create an item setting owner_id to victim's id
    payload = {
        "title": CANARY,
        "description": "owned by victim",
        "owner_id": str(victim_id),
    }
    url = f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/"
    resp_create = client.post(url, headers=headers_a, json=payload)
    assert resp_create.status_code == 200, "Item creation should succeed"
    data = resp_create.json()
    item_id = data["id"]

    # Attacker tries to read the item they just created
    resp_get = client.get(f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/{item_id}", headers=headers_a)
    # On base branch, attacker owns the item (owner_id forced to attacker) -> 200
    # On PR branch, item belongs to victim -> attacker gets 403
    assert resp_get.status_code == 200, (
        "Attacker should be able to read the item they created "
        "(owner_id should be ignored on base, but honored on PR leading to isolation)"
    )
    # Additionally, ensure the canary is present in the returned title
    assert resp_get.json()["title"] == CANARY

scenarios.root_cause: The regression stems from two changes: in `backend/app/models.py` line 81, `owner_id` was added as an optional field to `ItemCreate`, allowing clients to supply it; then in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` line 68, the server switched from forcing `owner_id = current_user.id` to `owner_id = item_in.owner_id or current_user.id`, so any provided value is honoured. This lets an authenticated user create items owned by arbitrary other users, widening `POST /items/` to hostile access for `superuser`, `user_a`, and `user_b` — a classic Broken Object Level Authorization / IDOR flaw [https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization) [https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html). The fix is to drop `owner_id` from `ItemCreate` and revert the route to `update={"owner_id": current_user.id}`.

import pytest
from app import crud
from app.models import ItemCreate
from tests.utils.user import authentication_token_from_email
from tests.utils.utils import random_lower_string

CANARY = "cnry-pr-mut-superuser-inverted"

def test_superuser_sees_all_items_including_other_users(
    client,
    db,
    normal_user_token_headers: dict[str, str],
    superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str],
) -> None:
    # Create a normal user item with the canary in the title
    # Get the normal user from token headers (we can fetch user via email)
    from app.core.config import settings
    email = settings.EMAIL_TEST_USER
    # authentication_token_from_email logs in and returns headers; we need user object.
    # Instead, we can create a user via helper.
    from tests.utils.user import create_random_user
    normal_user = create_random_user(db)
    assert normal_user.id is not None
    item_in = ItemCreate(
        title=f"{CANARY} {random_lower_string()}",
        description=random_lower_string(),
    )
    item = crud.create_item(session=db, item_in=item_in, owner_id=normal_user.id)

    # Login as superuser (fixture provides headers)
    response = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/items/",
        headers=superuser_token_headers,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    # Assuming response format: {"data": [...], ...} as seen in test_read_items
    items = data.get("data") if isinstance(data, dict) else data
    # Find item with canary in title
    found = any(CANARY in it.get("title", "") for it in items)
    assert found, f"Superuser did not see item with canary '{CANARY}'"

scenarios.root_cause: The inverted condition on line 21 (`if not current_user.is_superuser:`) swaps the authorization branches: superusers now receive the filtered query while regular users get the unfiltered `select(func.count()).select_from(Item)` and full item list, widening read access to all users (GET /items/ | user_a/user_b | base). This regresses I1 read-isolation by removing the superuser guard that enforced per-tenant scoping, effectively creating a broken object-level authorization bypass (CWE-639, API1:2023). Fix: revert to `if current_user.is_superuser:` so only superusers bypass tenant filtering.

import uuid

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from tests.utils.user import create_random_user, authentication_token_from_email
from tests.utils.item import create_random_item

CANARY = "cnry-pr-mut-update-no-owner"


def test_update_item_owner_isolation(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, normal_user_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    # Owner: create a random user and get token
    owner_user = create_random_user(db)
    owner_token = authentication_token_from_email(
        client=client, email=owner_user.email, db=db
    )
    # Attacker: use the existing normal user from fixture
    attacker_token = normal_user_token_headers

    # Owner creates an item with CANARY in title
    item_in = {
        "title": f"{CANARY} original",
        "description": "owned item",
    }
    resp = client.post(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/",
        headers=owner_token,
        json=item_in,
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    item = resp.json()
    item_id = item["id"]
    assert CANARY in item["title"]

    # Attacker attempts to update the item (should be forbidden)
    update_data = {"title": "hacked", "description": "tampered"}
    resp = client.put(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/{item_id}",
        headers=attacker_token,
        json=update_data,
    )
    # Base branch: expects 403
    assert resp.status_code == 403, f"Expected 403, got {resp.status_code}"
    # Fetch item again as owner to ensure unchanged
    resp = client.get(
        f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/items/{item_id}",
        headers=owner_token,
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    fetched = resp.json()
    # CANARY must still be present in title
    assert CANARY in fetched["title"], f"CANARY missing from title: {fetched['title']}"
